renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: frame_composition
  title: P-site reading frame per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library: the share of its P-sites that fall in each of the three reading frames, for one transcript region. It answers whether the footprints show the three-nucleotide periodicity of translating ribosomes.
    How to read: on the CDS, one frame should dominate, usually frame 0. The UTRs are not translated, so they stay close to a third per frame. A CDS that looks like the UTRs means the P-site offsets are wrong or the library lacks periodicity.
    Lines and annotations: a third per frame is the split of reads with no frame preference, a plain expectation of three frames and not a riboWaltz cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    rank_label: Region
    value_title: P-sites in the frame (%)
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    taxon: frame
    rank: region
    abundance: pct

- component: card
  id: frame_psites_card
  title: P-sites by frame
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of P-sites, the second number is the largest single count, and the bars rank the three frames by P-sites. It answers which frame holds most of the signal.
    How to read: pooled over regions the frames are mixed, so filter to the CDS to read the periodicity. One frame far ahead of the others means a phased library.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  column: count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: frame
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: P-sites, by frame

- component: table
  title: P-site frame counts
  description: |-
    Each row is a library, region and frame with its P-site count and share. It answers the exact numbers behind the bars.
    How to read: filter the region to the CDS and compare frame 0 with the other two.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: length_profile
  title: Footprint length distribution
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: the share of its reads at every read length that riboWaltz kept. It answers which footprint lengths dominate and whether libraries agree.
    How to read: ribosome-protected fragments form a narrow peak, and a broad or shifted distribution points at digestion or contamination problems. Libraries of one experiment should have the same peak. Several peaks can mark distinct ribosome conformations.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Read length (nt)
    y_title: Reads (%)
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: length
    y: pct

- component: figure
  id: length_line
  title: Reads by footprint length
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: the share of its reads at each read length. It answers the same question as the profile above with a plain chart.
    How to read: look for one narrow peak and for libraries whose peak sits at a different length from the rest.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: length
    y: pct
    color: sample
    labels:
      length: Read length (nt)
      pct: Reads (%)
      sample: Sample

- component: table
  title: Footprint length table
  description: |-
    Each row is a library and read length with its read count and share. It answers the exact numbers behind the lines.
    How to read: sort by share to find the dominant lengths.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: phasing_plane
  title: CDS share against frame 0 share
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: the share of its P-sites that fall in the CDS against the share of CDS P-sites in frame 0, sized by the number of P-sites, with one colour per library. It answers which libraries are both enriched on coding sequence and phased.
    How to read: good libraries sit top right. A point near the line, or with a negative margin, has no clear periodicity, which usually means the P-site offsets are wrong for that library. A point far left of its peers is dominated by UTR signal, as fragmented RNA would be.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line at a third marks the frame 0 share of a library with no frame preference. It is an arithmetic reference, an even split over three frames, and not a riboWaltz cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: P-sites in the CDS (%)
    y_title: CDS P-sites in frame 0 (%)
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_value: 33.3
    reference_label: No frame preference (one third)
  roles:
    x: cds_pct
    y: frame0_cds_pct
    label: sample
    size: psites
    color: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: library_record
  title: Library record
  description: |-
    Each record is one library with its quality readouts side by side. It answers how a single library scores on phasing, region share and footprint length.
    How to read: pick a library from the table or the plot to read its numbers together. A low frame 0 share with a negative margin and a CDS enrichment near one point to poor periodicity.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  kind: record_card
  config:
    labels:
      psites: P-sites assigned
      frame0_cds_pct: CDS P-sites in frame 0 (%)
      frame_bias: Frame 0 margin (points)
      cds_pct: P-sites in the CDS (%)
      utr5_pct: P-sites in the 5' UTR (%)
      utr3_pct: P-sites in the 3' UTR (%)
      cds_enrichment: CDS enrichment over length
      modal_length: Modal footprint length (nt)
      length_iqr: Footprint length spread (nt)
  roles:
    id: sample

- component: card
  id: frame0_card
  title: CDS P-sites in frame 0
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of CDS P-sites in the annotated reading frame, and the box shows the spread across libraries. It answers how well phased the libraries are.
    How to read: a third means no periodicity and well-phased footprints sit well above it. A long box means some libraries are phased and others are not.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  column: frame0_cds_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: frame_bias_card
  title: Frame 0 margin
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest margin of frame 0 over the next frame, in percentage points, and the second number is the median across libraries. It answers whether the worst library is still phased.
    How to read: a negative margin means another frame dominates, which usually means the P-site offsets are wrong for that library. riboWaltz publishes no minimum margin, so read it against the other libraries.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  column: frame_bias
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: lowest margin, with the median

- component: card
  id: cds_share_card
  title: P-sites in the CDS
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of P-sites on coding sequence, and the box shows the spread. It answers how well the libraries capture translation.
    How to read: footprints of translating ribosomes pile into the CDS. A library whose share follows the length of the CDS looks like fragmented RNA.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  column: cds_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: psites_card
  title: P-sites assigned
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of P-sites assigned over all libraries, and the second number is the median per library. It answers how much signal the run holds.
    How to read: libraries with far fewer P-sites than the median give noisy phasing and region shares, so read their numbers with care.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  column: psites
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: P-sites, with the median per library

- component: card
  id: modal_length_card
  title: Modal footprint length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of each library's most common read length, with the shortest and longest beside it. It answers whether libraries agree on the footprint length.
    How to read: libraries of one protocol should share the same mode. A library off by several nucleotides was digested or size-selected differently.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  column: modal_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: median, with the shortest and longest

- component: table
  title: Library quality table
  description: |-
    Each row is a library with its P-sites, phasing, region shares and footprint length. It answers the exact readouts behind the tiles of this tab.
    How to read: sort by frame 0 share to find the libraries that are least phased.

outputs.name: Metagene profile at the start codon

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: start_profile
  title: P-site signal around the start codon
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: its P-site signal at every nucleotide around the annotated start codon, summed over all transcripts. It answers whether footprints are phased along the coding sequence.
    How to read: Position 0 is the first nucleotide of the start codon. A peak there and a three-nucleotide saw-tooth along the CDS show a phased library. A flat or noisy line with no pattern means the offsets are wrong or the library has no periodicity.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical line at 0 marks the first nucleotide of the start codon, the origin of the distance axis, defined by the annotation riboWaltz uses.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    reference_x: 0
    reference_label: First nucleotide of the start codon
    x_title: Distance from the start codon (nt)
    y_title: Share of the window's P-site signal (%)
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: position
    y: signal

- component: table
  title: P-site signal around the start codon
  description: |-
    Each row is a library and a position relative to the start codon, with the share of the window's P-site signal. It answers the exact signal behind the lines.
    How to read: filter to one library and sort by position to follow its profile.

outputs.name: Metagene profile at the stop codon

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: stop_profile
  title: P-site signal around the stop codon
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: its P-site signal at every nucleotide around the annotated stop codon, summed over all transcripts. It answers whether footprints are phased along the coding sequence.
    How to read: Position 0 is the first nucleotide of the stop codon. The saw-tooth should run up to it and fade after it, where ribosomes release. A flat or noisy line with no pattern means the offsets are wrong or the library has no periodicity.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical line at 0 marks the first nucleotide of the stop codon, the origin of the distance axis, defined by the annotation riboWaltz uses.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    reference_x: 0
    reference_label: First nucleotide of the stop codon
    x_title: Distance from the stop codon (nt)
    y_title: Share of the window's P-site signal (%)
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: position
    y: signal

- component: table
  title: P-site signal around the stop codon
  description: |-
    Each row is a library and a position relative to the stop codon, with the share of the window's P-site signal. It answers the exact signal behind the lines.
    How to read: filter to one library and sort by position to follow its profile.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: region_composition
  title: P-sites per transcript region
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library: the share of its P-sites in the 5' UTR, CDS and 3' UTR. It answers whether the footprints accumulate on coding sequence.
    How to read: ribosome profiling data should define the CDS as the region with the highest share of reads. A library whose shares follow the length of each region behaves like fragmented RNA, not like translating ribosomes.
    Lines and annotations: where the scope also holds the share expected from random RNA fragmentation, it is the cumulative length of each region as a percentage, as defined by riboWaltz.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    rank_label: Scope
    value_title: Share of P-sites (%)
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    taxon: region
    rank: scope
    abundance: pct

- component: card
  id: region_enrichment_card
  title: CDS enrichment over length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median ratio of the CDS share of P-sites to the share its length alone would give, and the box shows the spread across libraries. It answers how strongly footprints favour coding sequence.
    How to read: a ratio of one means the footprints follow length, as fragmented RNA would, and higher values mean the CDS is enriched. Libraries far below their peers deserve a look.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LabTranslationalArchitectomics/riboWaltz/master/README.md
  column: enrichment
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('region') == 'CDS'
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: P-site region table
  description: |-
    Each row is a library and region with its P-site count, share, expected share and enrichment. It answers the exact numbers behind the bars.
    How to read: sort by enrichment to find the libraries that favour the CDS least.
